title: Introduce attribute-based RBAC filters and KMS region enforcement (audit-mode first)
author: Asha Mehta
description: Motivation: customers have asked for finer-grained RBAC controls that can express attribute-based allow/deny filters (for example tenant_id and data_residency_tag), and a safer rollout path for KMS region enforcement to prevent accidental cross-region key usage. This PR introduces an attribute-based RBAC (ABAC-style) extension to RBAC v2, a KMS region allowlist with explicit exemptions for service accounts, and a cluster-level audit-mode toggle so operators can evaluate effects before enforcement. Implementation summary: 1) RBAC: new policy predicates support 'attributes' on principals and resources (string equality, prefix match). Policies can reference request attributes (request.tenant, request.region, request.data_residency_tag). The policy engine evaluation path was extended to short-circuit and emit structured reasons for audits. 2) KMS region enforcement: new org-level KMS policy that validates encrypt/decrypt requests against key_region allowlists; keys outside allowed regions are blocked when enforcement is enabled. A service-account exemption list can be configured for cross-region infra keys. 3) Audit mode: a global and org-scoped audit_mode boolean defaults to true for 2 weeks after rollout; when audit_mode==true violations are logged to audit.log with severity 'policy_violation' but requests are allowed. 4) Migration: a migration script (tools/migrations/20241103_rbac_attr_kms.py) annotates existing policies with a minimal "attributes":[] field to be compatible. 5) Observability: new metrics (policy.eval.duration_ms, policy.violation.count, kms.region_block.count) and a Grafana dashboard JSON are included. 6) Docs: migration guide and operator runbook added under docs/security/rbac-attribute-guide.md and docs/security/kms-region-enforcement.md. Rollout plan: deploy with audit_mode=true in staging for one week, run policy audits and fix false positives, then flip enforcement for a small set of orgs, monitor metrics and error budget. Backwards compatibility: old RBAC v2 policies without attributes continue to work (attributes default to empty) so customers are not forced to change policies immediately.
